## Purpose
`approval_marker_observer.rs` (and 17 sibling `*Observer` modules under `hooks/`) implement the crate's `Observer` trait: pure side-effect, fire-and-forget recorders that MUST NOT return a verdict — per the project's own guard, blocking decisions live only in a `Check`. `approval_marker_observer.rs` demonstrates the discipline at its strictest: it records an unforgeable signal (a real user answer) only when every one of several independently-verifiable facts holds, and writes nothing on any doubt (fail-closed on the write, though the hook itself never blocks).

## Convention
Folder: apps/rt/src/hooks/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 18
`approval_marker_observer.rs` opens with a "why this exists" section naming the concrete forgeable/silent-failure defect it closes, then a numbered list of the facts that must ALL hold before the observer acts, each with its own sub-explanation. The observer writes a marker file only when the full conjunction holds; every other path is a documented no-op. `observe()` (implemented on a unit struct) returns `()` and every internal step degrades on failure rather than propagating an error — matching the CLAUDE.md guard that Observers never surface a verdict.

## How to apply
A new Observer is a unit struct implementing `Observer::observe(&self, input, ctx)` under the relevant `hooks/<family>/` directory, with a module header naming the field defect it closes and the exact conjunction of facts required before it writes anything. It never returns a `Verdict` and never calls into a `Check`'s evaluate path; any blocking decision belongs in a sibling `Check` instead.
